thread.title: The S&P 500 Faces Its Next Big Hurdle

title: The S&P 500 Faces Its Next Big Hurdle
text:
The S&P 500 Faces Its Next Big Hurdle By Feb. 6, 2019 11:56 a.m. ET Order Reprints Illustration by Michael Haddad Text size
The S&P 500 has risen 16% and added approximately $3.4 trillion in market capitalization since its Christmas Eve low . Now it is about to face its next big test—its 200-day moving average. the S&P 500 is just four points below that key technical level . Breaking that threshold would be a bullish signal for stocks, suggesting the market has completely climbed out of its recent trough.
The back story. Nothing has been able to stop the S&P 500 so far this year. After registering the best January in three decades, the index climbed 9% in 2019, and successfully pulled itself out of the correction territory, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has rallied 8.4%. The FAANG stocks, including Apple (AAPL) and Amazon.com (AMZN), plus Microsoft (MSFT) together have contributed to 20% of that gain, noted Mike O’Rourke from JonesTrading , but they are not the only gainers. The breadth of this rally is pretty healthy. As of Tuesday’s close, there are only 30, or 6%, of S&P 500 companies in negative territory this year, O’Rourke wrote in a Tuesday note.
The plot twist. After breaking a series of tactical resistance levels, the S&P 500 is now approaching its 200-day moving average. If the index can move above the threshold, it is yet another sign that the market has strong upward momentum. Another bullish signal: The S&P 500 14-day relative strength index (RSI)—a momentum indicator that evaluate overbought or oversold conditions by measuring recent price changes—has reached the highest level since mid September, Peter Boockvar of Bleakley Advisory Group . The rally is due to multiple tailwinds in the market, says Boockvar, including relief from the Fed’s dovish shift, hopes for a China deal, solid economic data, and better-than-expected earnings.
Going forward. Despite the impressive run, O’Rourke reminds investors be aware what’s driving the rally and cautious about liquidity in market. He suspect the algorithm-driven computer models, knowing no fear, have fostered the “short-term extreme moves” and the current pace might not be sustainable in longer term. It might be time to temper expectations.
